deviations.description: VERIFICATION.json's V103 (and, by the same authoring pattern, U003's V303 and U004's V403 in the same package) referenced infra/docker/scripts/wlt-migration-probes.ps1, which does not exist anywhere in the repository. Corrected V103's command in this unit to the real, already-registered migration path (guard:migration-manifest-drift + runtime:wlt:migrate + runtime:wlt:smoke) before Freeze, per governing prompt PHASE A rule that a Package's internal defect blocks Product write until fixed. V303/V403 were NOT touched: they belong to U003/U004, which are out of scope for this round; flagged here as a reopen trigger for whoever executes those units.

tools/scripts/generate-migration-manifest.mjs recomputes a different sha256 for every one of the 72 pre-existing HISTORICAL_IMMUTABLE/ACTIVE manifest entries than what is currently committed in services/wlt/database/migrations/manifest.json, even with the tree at HEAD and no migration files touched (verified by stashing this unit's new migration file and regenerating against a clean checkout). The manifest-drift guard (tools/guards/migration-manifest-drift-gate.mjs) does not use the generator's algorithm -- it independently accepts any of raw/LF-normalized/CRLF-normalized digests per file -- so this generator/guard mismatch does not block CI or this unit's V103. To avoid an unauthorized rewrite of 72 immutable hash entries, this unit registered wlt-908/909/910 by hand-appending exactly one new ordinal entry per migration (matching the LF-normalized digest the generator would itself produce for a from-scratch file) rather than running the generator. Root cause not diagnosed further; out of this unit's scope, flagged for governance/tooling ownership with a reopen trigger.

U001's own required checks (V101-V104) do not depend on this guard; pnpm --dir services/wlt run lint does, and therefore currently fails for this pre-existing, unrelated reason -- not because of anything in this unit's delta.

U001-T003 built the ledger-backed opening-balance/correction mechanism and a canonical read projection (PostOpeningBalance, PostFinancialCorrection, GetWalletLedgerProjection in services/wlt/backend/internal/ledger/opening_balance.go) but did NOT migrate the legacy wlt_wallets writers below, per this round's explicit scope ruling (COD/payout lifecycle rewrites belong to U003/U004, not U001, and U001's mustNotChange forbids touching COD/payout state machines). Every site below is a pre-existing direct SQL mutation of wlt_wallets (available/pending/held/earned/settled/paid_total_balance_minor_units), parallel to wlt_ledger_accounts.balance_minor_units, confirmed present at STARTING_REMOTE_SHA (none were introduced by this unit's delta):

Reopen trigger: confirm ownership with product authority before U003/U004 execution.
- services/wlt/backend/internal/wallet/repository.go (1 site: EnsureWalletForOperatorContextTx) -- this is zero-balance row creation only (wallet lifecycle bootstrap), not a balance-changing write; left as-is, no reopen trigger needed.

None of these sites double-counts against this unit's new opening-balance/correction mechanism: they operate exclusively on wlt_wallets, never on wlt_ledger_accounts via PostOpeningBalance/PostFinancialCorrection, so no order/value can be affected by both paths simultaneously in the current delta. This finding does not rise to BLOCKER per this unit's diagnosis, because every writer is owned by a named later unit (U003/U004) with a coverage entry already IN_SCOPE for it -- it is recorded as a reopen trigger, not left silent.
